style.vernacular: Dense hillside city of reinforced-concrete apartment blocks (apartman) of 4 to 8 storeys finished in cream, ochre or pale-grey render with balconies and flat or low-pitched roofs topped by water tanks and satellite dishes; surviving 19th-century stone and brick buildings with arched windows; old Ottoman timber houses painted in ochre, red and cream on the Bosphorus shore and in Balat; domed stone Ottoman mosques with pencil minarets and clay-tile or lead roofs; glass towers in Levent and Maslak. Clay (Marseille) tile hip roofs on villas and older houses.
style.ornament: Ottoman domes and semi-domes with slender pencil minarets; arched stone windows and polychrome brick-and-stone banding (Byzantine and Ottoman); timber cumba bay windows overhanging the street; Neoclassical and Balyan-family palace facades with pilasters and cornices; Iznik tile panels; balcony-fronted apartment blocks.

sources.what: Ottoman classical domed mosques, 19th-century Western influence (Balyan family), early 20th-century apartment blocks, concrete and glass-curtain modern buildings
